thread:
maria-ml: quick heads-up — putting this here before i forget. after the tiny normalization change in the eval runner (lowercase + strip punctuation) we see a reproducible NDCG@10 drop on the mteb-like rerank suite for the new quantized-embed model. not catastrophic but consistent: ~0.39 -> 0.33.

samir-research: can you paste the exact command you ran and the small diff? want to reproduce locally.

maria-ml: repro command: `./tools/eval_runner --suite rerank_mteb --model quantized-embed-v2 --use-normalization true --seed 42 --workers 8`

normalization snippet we added in runner preprocessing:
```
def normalize(q):
    q = q.lower()
    q = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", "", q)  # strip punctuation
    q = q.strip()
    return q
```

chris-qa: FYI the CI job `runner-eval-embeddings` also flaked earlier today — job requeued once and then passed. might be unrelated but worth checking for nondeterminism.

evalbot: auto-report: run_id=2026-03-20-09:42:id187
baseline(unnormalized): ndcg@10=0.3894, mrr=0.4121, recall@100=0.862
normalized: ndcg@10=0.3330, mrr=0.3918, recall@100=0.857
delta(ndcg@10) = -14.5%  (absolute -0.0564)

jenni-eng: interesting. two hypotheses:
1) the embed model was trained on cased/punctuated data -> normalization collapses signal that helps reranking high-confidence items.
2) tokenization mismatch: our normalize() changes character sequence differently than the tokenizer used by the embedding model (sentencepiece/subword), so the same query maps to a different embedding manifold.

suggestion: add a toggle in harness to run `tokenizer.normalize_text()` (model-backed normalization) vs the generic runner normalization. also run ab test: quantized vs non-quantized under both normalization modes.

samir-research: can you show an example query that flips order? curious to see if it's punctuation or case-driven.

maria-ml: example (original -> normalized):
Original: "How do I reset my account? (forgot password)"
Normalized: "how do i reset my account forgot password"

Top results (baseline): [docA, docC, docB]  (ndcg contribution high)
Top results (normalized): [docC, docA, docB]

docA contains an exact short-span "reset my account" in title with parentheses in source PDF; maybe punctuation anchors helped.

chris-qa: another angle — the rerank runner caches prefix embeddings for multistep queries. if normalization changes the prefix key format we might get cache misses or stale hits when switching code paths in CI. i saw logs like `kvcache: hit 0/46` vs baseline `hit 23/46`. can someone grep kvcache stats for these runs?

maria-ml: good catch. i dumped the kvcache stats for the two runs:
baseline: `kvcache_hits=22,kvcache_misses=24`
normalized: `kvcache_hits=2,kvcache_misses=44`

that aligns — when we normalize text we change caching keys and lose speed + locality which can affect batched rerank ordering because latency/ordering heuristics differ. weird but plausible.

jenni-eng: plan proposal:
- add `--normalization-mode` flag with choices `raw|simple|tokenizer` in eval harness
- add small unit test that compares tokenized sequences between runner and model.tokenizer for 50 random samples
- add CI matrix entry: run rerank_mteb once with `simple` and once with `tokenizer` on a small subset (quick smoke)
- clear kvcache between runs and record hits/misses in CI artifact

samir-research: i can own the unit test + the ab-run harness wiring. will add a small dataset fixture with edge-case queries (parentheses, dashes, emojis).

chris-qa: i'll add the CI job matrix and artifact capture; will also add the kvcache assertion threshold (hits shouldn't drop >50% between runs without reason).

evalbot: ticket created: INF-2342 - "eval-runner: add normalization-mode toggle + kvcache smoke tests" assigned to samir-research, chris-qa. CI job created: `ci/eval/harness-normalization-matrix`

maria-ml: thanks team. immediate short-term rollback: i'm going to revert the simple normalization in the nightly full-run until we have the toggle. long-term follow-up per jenni/samir/chris plan. i'll post PR links shortly. :thumbsup:

jenni-eng: i'll also add a note in the onboarding doc about tokenizer-aware preprocessing — we should warn model owners to include a tokenizer-normalization helper when they onboard models.

maria-ml: awesome — assigning follow-ups: samir = unit tests + harness flag; chris = CI matrix + kvcache capture; jenni = docs blurb.

maria-ml: leaving this thread open for any other quick observations, otherwise i'll close after PRs land.
